questions.stem: The Doppler effect is the apparent change in:

options.explanation: Wave speed stays fixed by the medium.

options.text: observed wavelength and frequency from a moving source
options.explanation: Both observed quantities shift when the source moves relative to the observer.
The effect concerns wavelength and frequency, not size of swing.
The source emits unchanged; the shift is observed.

questions.stem: A stationary siren emits wavefronts that spread:

options.explanation: That pattern needs a moving source.
Sirens emit in all directions.
With no motion, every direction is equivalent.
The wavefronts spread as expanding rings.

questions.stem: An observer stands in front of an approaching siren. Compared with the emitted wave, the observer receives:

options.text: a longer wavelength and a lower frequency
options.explanation: That is what an observer behind hears.
The whole point of the effect is the apparent shift.

options.text: a shorter wavelength and a lower frequency
options.explanation: The pairing violates the fixed wave speed.

options.text: a shorter wavelength and a higher frequency
options.explanation: Wavefronts bunch up ahead of the motion.

questions.stem: After a police car passes and drives away, the observed pitch an observer hears:

options.text: drops, because the wavefronts stretch behind the car
options.explanation: Receding sources give longer apparent wavelengths and lower frequencies.

options.text: rises, because the car gains distance
options.explanation: Distance alone does not raise pitch; the stretching pattern lowers it.

options.text: stays the same as when it approached
options.explanation: Approach and recession give opposite shifts.
The sound continues, just at lower pitch.

questions.stem: Light from a galaxy appears redder than emitted. This shows the galaxy is:

options.explanation: Approach would shift light bluer, not redder.
A stationary source shows no shift.
Redder light means longer apparent wavelength, the recession signature.

options.text: emitting at a lower frequency by nature
options.explanation: The effect is apparent, caused by motion, not a changed emitter.

questions.stem: State what happens to the observed wavelength of a wave from a source moving towards you.
questions.modelAnswer: The observed wavelength appears shorter, because the wavefronts bunch together ahead of the moving source.

questions.stem: State the everyday example of the Doppler effect heard in traffic.
questions.modelAnswer: A siren or engine drops from high pitch to low pitch as the vehicle passes and recedes.

questions.stem: Explain why the wave speed does not change in the Doppler effect even though the observed frequency does.
questions.modelAnswer: Wave speed is fixed by the properties of the medium, not by the source motion, so the only way the pattern can change is in its spacing and arrival rate, which is why wavelength and frequency shift together and oppositely.

questions.stem: An ambulance drives past a pedestrian at constant speed with its siren on. Describe and explain how the pitch heard changes from before the ambulance reaches the pedestrian to after it has passed.
questions.modelAnswer: Before it passes, the ambulance approaches so wavefronts bunch and the pitch sounds high; after it passes, the ambulance recedes so wavefronts stretch and the pitch drops, even though the siren emits at one constant frequency throughout.
